notes: Fresh child per case, generated fixtures outside measured child; no concurrent suite during response runs.
Historical targets were input/cancel <=100ms and matching frame <=150ms, but historical handled was callback-before-write; they do not establish natural scheduling latency.

Historical baseline frame used flush completion; historical candidate used renderNow and next generation without state matching. Current reviewRound separately measures accepted state and matching natural frame.
Decode interval for a terminated worker ends at its exit; native function completion/object count and peak WASM at termination are unknown.
RSS peak is actual process resourceUsage.maxRSS (includes worker native memory); controlled GC is diagnostic only.
PNG fixture path has no format conversion. Parent function wrappers measure base64 and I/O; decode start/end diagnostics originate in the actual worker.

naturalDefinition.planned: decoder entry +5ms; oversize cases after rejection
naturalDefinition.callbackAt: timer callback, before input.write; handled retained as legacy alias
naturalDefinition.inputArrived: real CustomEditor.handleInput entry for probe key
naturalDefinition.processed: after real handler changed text to PROBE_BASEx, or cleared editor and draft
naturalDefinition.frame: write completion of a concrete frame whose nextScreen contained the expected state, matched again by exact frame data at the terminal queue sink
naturalDefinition.scheduling: no probe renderNow or flush; only setup/cleanup flush outside probe measurement; simulated async sink, no desktop compositor

acceptance.nativeDesktop: not executed; known unavailable interface not retried
acceptance.cleanup: prior policy rejection preserved; no retry or bypass

limits: One child per scenario: controlled observations, not broad latency percentiles or all terminals/formats.
Header/byte rejection happens before decoder; over-limit probes are not decode-window evidence.
Termination interval ends at worker exit; exact interrupted native-function completion/object count/WASM peak unknown.
Frame matching reads the production alt-screen prepared buffer in diagnostic code; it measures simulated sink completion, not desktop paint.
20.4% remains the original specific visual-tail allocation sample, not machine/TUI speed; unchanged drain receives no credit.
